names.note: Name page of days.pravoslavie.ru for this memory is «Антонина (Брянских), мц.»: «мц.» is a rank word and is stripped and the surname kept, the day line itself giving only «Антонины». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

death.note: The day line closes «(1937)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 декабря ст. ст. — «Мц. Антонины (1937).»

attestations.note: The day’s seventh and last entry, and THE LINE AND THE NAME PAGE ARE ALL THERE IS: no life page stands behind it. The line gives her no grade beyond «Мц.», martyr, so `martyr` is the source’s own word and `new-martyr` is written as this corpus writes it for this calendar’s twentieth-century entries; no `office` was invented. A Cyrillic grep for «Брянских» over every `saint.json` returns `parthenius-bryanskikh` and `mitrophan-kornitsky` — another forename in the first and the surname in prose in the second — and `ls -d saints/antonin*` returns fifteen folders, none of them this woman. `fk.mjs` on the stored form returns NONE. The day page carries four hymns — three for the protomartyr Stephen and one for the venerable Theodore — and none under this name.
